title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system; HR organization charts
what_it_shows: A holding company (SEC registrant) with three subsidiaries: Cris Santos Transformer Company, LLC; Cris Santos Electric, LLC; Cris Santos Grid Engineering, Inc. Corporate shared services sit in the parent. Organization charts show the Group CISO, the Group OT security director reporting to the Group CISO, the three division security and compliance leads, and plant OT leads at P1 to P7 reporting to the Director of OT engineering. The P8 chart shows a plant manager and maintenance staff and no OT security role

title: Group: HR headcount by division and role
source_system: Group HR system (SYS-G5)
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Transformer Manufacturing about 24,000 (including about 110 Grid Products engineers and about 60 FMS engineers and data scientists), Electric Utility about 9,000, Grid Engineering about 7,000 in 40 offices in 18 states, corporate about 5,000. Specialist teams: 8 OT security staff and 6 NERC compliance staff. Job descriptions and performance goals for engineering, operations and control owner roles include security duties

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger (SYS-G4); FY2025 Form 10-K
what_it_shows: Revenue about $18.0 billion: Transformer Manufacturing about $9.6 billion, Electric Utility about $6.0 billion, Grid Engineering about $2.4 billion from external clients. Exports are about 8% of Transformer Manufacturing revenue (utilities in Canada, Mexico and the Caribbean). Grid Engineering billed the Electric Utility about $310 million under the 2020 intercompany services agreement

title: Group: SEC disclosure records
source_system: SEC filings; disclosure committee records
what_it_shows: The FY2025 annual report includes the Regulation S-K Item 106 disclosure. The disclosure committee charter covers cybersecurity incidents. The charter and committee records list no pre-agreed materiality factors for an incident that stops production, and no committee exercise with plant data is recorded

title: Group: board risk committee minutes and 2026 risk strategy
source_system: Board portal
what_it_shows: Quarterly cyber risk reports to the board risk committee through 2026-03; the board audit committee oversees internal audit. The 2026 risk strategy, with risk objectives agreed by the committee and the division presidents, was approved in 2026-03. Division presidents own risk acceptance at Moderate

title: Group: ERM risk profile, 2025 risk registers and program metrics
source_system: GRC tool
what_it_shows: Group and division 2025 risk registers on one SP 800-30 scale, rolled up per NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1. Fraud risk appears in the ERM profile. A program metrics dashboard (patch latency, mean time to detect, OT monitoring coverage) is reviewed each quarter

title: Group: internal audit charter and 2026 audit plan
source_system: Internal audit records
what_it_shows: Internal audit reports to the board audit committee and neither designs nor operates the controls it assesses. The 2026 plan assesses the common controls marked for 2026 in the common control catalog once and samples division controls; OT tests may be co-sourced. Fraud risk is part of the audit plan

title: Group: policy library and acknowledgments
source_system: Group policy repository; intranet; learning system
what_it_shows: Group policies POL-01 to POL-05 v2026, approved 2026-03-24 and aligned to CSF 2.0, published on the intranet. Staff acknowledge the code of conduct and the POL-05 rules of behavior at hire and every year; the sanctions procedure under POL-01 has a sanctions log. The Group AI Standard was adopted in 2026-03 and the Group AI council chartered

title: Group: group standards register
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Standards in force, each with owner and review date: identity, identifier, password, session, remote access, logging, configuration management, continuity, planning, and assessment and authorization standards, and the group OT security standard based on SP 800-82 Rev. 3. Identifiers are unique and never reused; passwords follow length and breached-password screening rules

title: Group: division supplements and the Grid Engineering 2023 standards
source_system: Group policy repository; division document libraries
what_it_shows: Electric Utility supplement v2026, aligned 2026-02-27, maps each group policy to the CIP program document that implements it. The Transformer Manufacturing supplement (2025 edition) covers plants P1 to P7 and has no section on P8 or AI use cases. Grid Engineering has no supplement: its 2023 division standards, last aligned 2023-04, set 90-day platform log retention, allow personal USB drives on commissioning laptops if scanned, allow shared accounts on settings tools, use a 3-level severity scale, and leave client notices to the project manager

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: GRC tool
what_it_shows: Catalog of 104 group common controls (2025 edition) with provider and owner. Inheritance matrices: Transformer Manufacturing (2025, IT systems; plant OT follows the group OT standard) and Electric Utility (2025, IT systems only, used as CIP evidence). No inheritance matrix was provided for Grid Engineering

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication, federation and access policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: 45,000 unique workforce identities. MFA with number matching for all workforce users; phishing-resistant hardware keys for administrators; lockout after 10 failed attempts with risk-based blocking; re-authentication for privileged elevation and every 10 hours; replay-resistant federation protocols for every group application, the GEPS, the client project platform, and the AMI head end and CIS. Conditional access admits covered systems and the GEPS from managed devices only. Remote workforce access runs through the zero-trust access service over TLS 1.2 or higher. SYS-G1 is not used inside the Electric Utility's Electronic Security Perimeters

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance configuration and Q1 2026 certification
source_system: Identity governance console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events; terminated users disabled within 4 hours; accounts inactive 60 days disabled; temporary and emergency accounts expire after 30 days; accounts flagged high risk disabled within 1 hour on request. Unique identities for all users of covered systems. The Q1 2026 quarterly certification of workforce and privileged access, including FMS roles, was completed. The 20 GEPS service accounts are not in identity governance or in the certification

title: Group: PAM role list, account inventory and session records
source_system: Privileged access management console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Named security administrators hold GEPS role administration through PAM; administrators use separate privileged accounts; privileged GEPS and database access is granted just in time with approval and session recording; ERP vendor support connects only through PAM with per-ticket approval, MFA and recording

title: Group: corporate directory trust configuration
source_system: Corporate directory admin console
what_it_shows: A two-way trust links the corporate domain to the P8 legacy directory domain, in place since the 2025-09 acquisition (AQ-25). P8 user and plant accounts sit in the legacy domain, outside SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: SIEM data source list and detection rules
source_system: SIEM and OT monitoring console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC. Sources: SYS-G1 (including account lifecycle and privileged function use), cloud platform logs, EDR, GEPS security events, landing-zone and site firewalls, OT DMZ logs at P1 to P7, and passive OT network sensors at P1 to P7 and at the TCC and backup TCC Electronic Access Points. Not in the source list: GEPS APS and integration hub job logs, GEPS service account sign-ins, FMS application logs of cross-tenant queries, any P8 source, and OT sensors at the DCC (DCC firewall logs are sent). User behavior analytics on SYS-G1, the GEPS and PLM; correlation rules and SOAR playbooks; a log-source loss alert within 1 hour; remote session rules. Network detection inspects inbound and outbound traffic at the landing-zone hub with no baseline for hub-to-plant traffic

title: Group: SOC case records and metrics, 2025 to 2026-03
source_system: SOC case management system (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Every incident is tracked as a case; cases are triaged and validated within 30 minutes on the group severity scale, and OT alerts from P1 to P7 are analyzed with SOAR playbooks. Grid Engineering cases carry the division's own 3-level severity

title: Group: EDR coverage report and policy
source_system: EDR console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: EDR on all IT endpoints and servers (including GEPS servers, about 900 field laptops and the Grid Engineering offices and laptops), cloud hosts, and OT DMZ servers at P1 to P7. Agents update automatically; downloads and attachments are scanned in real time with weekly full scans; endpoint policy blocks unapproved software installs. P8 servers and HMIs are not enrolled. Software inventory is collected from endpoint and cloud tooling

title: Group: vulnerability scan, patch and allowlisting reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner and patch management consoles (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Weekly authenticated scans of IT and cloud hosts, including GEPS hosts and covered systems; critical findings remediated within 15 days; ERP vendor patches each quarter; OEM-approved OT patches at P1 to P7 in each maintenance window; application allowlisting on HMIs and engineering workstations at P1 to P7. P8 servers and the P8 MES are outside the scanning scope, and no P8 patch records exist

title: Group: threat intelligence and advisory log
source_system: SOC threat intelligence records (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Threat intelligence from commercial feeds and the sector ISAC. CISA ICS advisories are reviewed daily, including advisories for transformer plant equipment and plant interface products

title: Group: incident response plan v5, plant OT playbooks and exercise reports
source_system: Group SOC document library
what_it_shows: IR plan v5 covers IT incidents with group playbooks, a ransomware playbook and an evidence handling procedure. Plant OT playbooks for P1 to P7 define the isolation point at each OT DMZ and a plant restart procedure that verifies restored controllers against backups. The plan has no cross-division notification steps, no plant restart coordination, no P8 content, and no link from the ransomware playbook to GEPS scheduling recovery; OEMs are not named in it. Exercise reports for 2025 and 2026-Q1 record quarterly technical playbook tests and no cross-division or P8 exercise. Customer communication templates cover delivery delays; none covers storm-season allocation changes after an incident. Incident severity criteria follow the group scale

title: Group: cyber insurance tower and forensic retainer
source_system: Contract management system
what_it_shows: Group cyber insurance tower with an incident response panel that includes an OT-capable forensic firm, a retainer agreement with that firm, and business continuity coverage terms

title: Group: monthly security reports and 2026 penetration test report
source_system: Group CISO reporting; penetration test vendor report
what_it_shows: Monthly continuous monitoring reports on configuration, vulnerabilities and security events. The 2026-03 penetration test covered the GEPS web tier and the supplier portal; the integration hub and its plant interfaces were outside its scope

title: Group: cloud inventory and landing-zone IAM configuration
source_system: Cloud provider consoles and asset inventory (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: One landing zone per provider with division accounts. Provider A: corporate hub, the GEPS, the data platform (AI-001, AI-002, AI-004) and the Electric Utility EAM. Provider B: the FMS, the Grid Engineering client project platform, the GEPS disaster recovery environment and reporting copy, and the immutable backup vault. Cloud resources are inventoried automatically. IAM roles are federated from SYS-G1 and scoped to division accounts; no standing cross-division administrator roles

title: Group: guardrail compliance report, hardened images and endpoint baseline
source_system: Guardrail policy service; image catalog (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Guardrails and service control policies apply to every division account; deviations are reported weekly. Hardened image catalog and baselines with unneeded services and ports disabled; GEPS application configuration is version-controlled; software licenses tracked in a central register; managed workstations lock after 10 minutes idle

title: Group: hub network, firewall, edge and WAN configuration
source_system: Firewall management and network documentation (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Landing-zone hub firewalls deny by default and allow by exception, with rule review records; site firewalls are monitored by the SOC. External access points are limited to the hub and the supplier portal edge; provider denial-of-service protection and a web application firewall front the GEPS; the public website and the supplier portal edge sit in separate segments; network policy limits connections between GEPS tiers. SD-WAN reaches plants and offices over two carriers with cellular backup; GEPS traffic to P1 to P7 terminates in each OT DMZ. Network diagrams on file

title: Group: key management, encryption settings and TLS scan
source_system: Key management service; TLS scanner (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Customer-managed keys in the provider key services, rotated yearly, with approved algorithms. Databases, cloud storage, backups and laptops are encrypted at rest with group-managed keys; laptops use full-disk encryption with remote wipe. Endpoints accept TLS 1.2 or higher only

title: Group: immutable backup vault configuration and backup reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Backup service (provider B, SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Daily immutable backups of GEPS databases and application servers, the FMS, TDMS and the client project platform to the provider B vault, which uses a separate backup identity and group-managed keys; daily integrity checks; restore records for sampled FMS and project platform data sets. Nightly MES database copies from P1 to P7 reach the vault. No P8 system is backed up to the vault

title: Group: central log archive configuration
source_system: Log archive account (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Write-once log archive in a separate account that only SOC log administrators manage; storage scales automatically; GEPS audit logs searchable for 1 year and archived for 7 years; all components use the provider time service

title: Group: cloud provider SOC 2 reports
source_system: Cloud provider compliance portals
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports for providers A and B, covering physical security and media sanitization in their data centers, and their published shared responsibility descriptions. The provider B report is reviewed each year

title: Group: training completion and role-based training records
source_system: Learning management system
what_it_shows: 2025 annual awareness training completed by 96% of workforce users and 97% of office staff, with a shop-floor version delivered at shift meetings; the course covers insider threat; quarterly phishing exercises. Role-based OT security training for controls engineers at P1 to P7 and none recorded at P8; GEPS administrator and key-user training; no OT-aware training recorded for integration hub engineers. Annual contingency training for recovery staff and incident response training for responders and liaisons. Records kept 6 years

title: Group: HR screening procedure and records
source_system: Group HR system (SYS-G5)
what_it_shows: Background checks before access for all workforce members. Group HR runs the checks for engineers who need client or affiliate TCC access and sends an attestation that does not list which checks were performed

title: Group: supplier master, tiering register, SCRM plan and purchasing procedure
source_system: ERP supplier master (SYS-G4); third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: About 2,400 suppliers tiered by criticality; 46 tier 1 suppliers, including the ERP vendor, the cloud providers and the EDI provider, reviewed each year; critical suppliers assessed before award; OT and product component suppliers reviewed only at onboarding; the TMU contract manufacturer is audited every 2 years. The group SCRM plan (2025) covers IT, OT and product suppliers. The purchasing procedure sets supplier security requirements. Supplier files for the TMU contract manufacturer and the OEMs serving P8 name no security contact or duties

title: Group: contract templates and key supplier contract terms
source_system: Contract management system
what_it_shows: IT and cloud contract templates include security requirements, supported-software terms and incident notice. The ERP vendor and EDI provider contracts require incident notice within 24 hours; ERP vendor and integrator personnel requirements are in their contracts. The AMI and CIS vendor contracts carry 72-hour incident notice

title: Group: SaaS vendor SOC 2 reports on file
source_system: Third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: SOC 2 reports on file for the identity platform vendor, the ERP vendor, the EAM vendor and the AMI and CIS vendors

title: Group: AI use-case discovery
source_system: Procurement records; SaaS discovery; model registry on the group data platform
what_it_shows: AI found: AI-001 demand forecasting (in production since 2024), AI-002 predictive maintenance with vendor models (in production since 2025), AI-003 FMS asset-health analytics, AI-004 load forecasting (model replaced in 2025), AI-005 enterprise generative AI assistant pilot (3,000 users), AI-006 Grid Engineering design assistant pilot (120 engineers), AI-007 weld and paint vision inspection (P4; P5 pilot), AI-008 coding assistant for the 110 firmware developers, and AI-009 invoice matching in the GEPS. AI-001 and AI-002 went into production before the Group AI Standard, and no independent validation record exists for either. Model registry entries exist for AI-001, AI-002 and AI-004

title: Group: web proxy logs for public generative AI sites
source_system: Web proxy (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Users on plant office networks reach public generative AI sites; public AI tools are blocked at some plants and not at others; the enterprise assistant is the approved tool. The logs do not show what users paste

title: Group: legacy group file server share inventory
source_system: File server administration (SYS-G6)
what_it_shows: Legacy on-premises file servers in the group data center with broad share permissions hold HR exports that include Social Security numbers and about 1,400 Grid Engineering closed project folders from 2016 to 2023

title: Group: intercompany agreements
source_system: Contract management system
what_it_shows: 2019 intercompany supply agreement (transformers and spares to the Electric Utility) and 2020 intercompany services agreement (Grid Engineering design, settings and commissioning): neither has a security schedule or the Electric Utility's CIP-013-2 or CIP-011-3 terms

title: GEPS: user, role and service account exports
source_system: GEPS administration console (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: About 16,500 named users (about 11,000 in Transformer Manufacturing) and 1,900 supplier portal users. Roles come from the SYS-G1 role catalog by company code and plant, approved by each company-code data owner under the GEPS access runbook; administrative transactions are limited to admin roles; only the release team can move transports to production. 20 service accounts: 6 for the integration hub and 14 for batch jobs, created by the GEPS team. The 6 hub accounts can write work orders and bills of materials to all 8 plant MES and use static keys older than 1 year. Sessions end after 30 minutes idle (15 minutes on shop-floor kiosks) and after 10 hours; a system use notice is shown at sign-in

title: GEPS: integration hub interface list and interface agreements register
source_system: Integration hub console; GEPS interface register
what_it_shows: The integration hub is the only approved path between the GEPS and the plant MES. Flows to P1 to P7 terminate in each OT DMZ under per-plant interface agreements (2024). The hub list shows a direct link to the P8 legacy MES, which has no interface agreement and no entry, endpoint or batch account in the interface register. EDI runs through the EDI network provider and 2 direct core steel supplier links with no interconnection agreement. A 2023 intercompany data agreement covers the Electric Utility EAM interface. Interface specifications include input validation

title: GEPS: architecture, configuration and audit settings
source_system: GEPS architecture repository; application and audit configuration
what_it_shows: Web, application and database tiers, the APS engine and the integration hub in provider A; the supplier portal behind the group customer identity service with MFA; a read-only reporting copy in provider B refreshed every 4 hours. Audit generation is on for all modules and the database: sign-ins, role changes, master data changes with before-and-after values, schedule releases and export screening overrides. Session tokens are bound to the session; file integrity monitoring on application servers and signed transport packages; all components on supported versions; design review records; the configuration management plan is in the platform runbook

title: GEPS: change records, Q1 2026
source_system: GEPS change management (change advisory board)
what_it_shows: Changes approved by the change advisory board with SOX approvals and tested in a quality environment before production; each change carries a security impact analysis; interface changes that affect plant MES carry no review by plant OT engineers; emergency changes reviewed within 2 business days

title: GEPS: contingency plan v3, DR architecture and 2026-02 DR test report
source_system: GEPS continuity library
what_it_shows: Contingency plan v3 covers database failover and finance recovery and is cross-referenced to the group crisis plan; it sets no order for restoring APS, the integration hub and plant interfaces and no steps for plants to re-synchronize their MES. A warm DR environment in provider B with database replication (RPO about 15 minutes). The 2026-02 DR test restored the finance modules only. The restore test log covers finance tables; APS and the integration hub have not been restored in a test. The recovery runbook covers the database and finance

title: GEPS: export screening and records retention settings
source_system: GEPS export screening module; GEPS retention schedule
what_it_shows: Every export order is screened against U.S. government restricted-party lists before release; export records and financial records are kept 7 years; a manual fallback screening procedure using the government screening list exists, with no drill on record

title: Transformer Manufacturing: OT asset inventory export, P1 to P7
source_system: OT monitoring console and OT asset inventory (SYS-M2)
what_it_shows: About 3,850 OT assets at P1 to P7 (PLCs, CNC core cutting lines, winding machines, drying ovens, vacuum oil processing, robotic welding, paint lines, crane controls, HMIs and engineering workstations), discovered passively, each with owner and criticality; OT software is recorded. No P8 asset is in the inventory

title: Transformer Manufacturing: plant OT program records, P1 to P7
source_system: OT program records; IT/OT firewall exports; OEM remote access gateway console
what_it_shows: The 2023 to 2025 plant OT program built OT DMZs with MES application servers and historian replicas at P1 to P7, deny-by-default IT/OT firewalls and zoned plant networks. OEM access at P1 to P7 runs through the central gateway with MFA, per-request approval and session recording, and session records are reviewed. Configuration baselines for OT DMZ servers; OT change board records; automated daily controller program backups and nightly MES database backups to the plant backup appliance and the vault; controller program restore tests; manual shutdown procedures and paper traveler procedures for up to 3 days of production

title: Transformer Manufacturing: P8 acquisition and integration records
source_system: Integration program office records
what_it_shows: P8 (South Carolina; distribution transformers and voltage regulators) was acquired 2025-09 as AQ-25. The integration plan schedules migration of the P8 legacy MES to the standard MES behind an OT DMZ. Acquisition due diligence did not include a check for covered telecommunications equipment. The P8 MES is backed up to local disk; P8 controller programs are copied ad hoc (last full set 2026-03); P8 has no paper production procedure. OEM support contracts are in place

title: Transformer Manufacturing: TMU firmware build, signing and release records
source_system: Code repositories (SaaS); build servers; customer download portal (SYS-M5)
what_it_shows: 7 firmware lines and the configuration software. Development standard: code review, static analysis, two-person review on release branches, and signed releases with SHA-256 hashes published on the download portal. The signing key is held in a software keystore on a build server in the group data center; the build servers are in the corporate domain. SBOMs exist for 3 of the 7 firmware lines; the other lines keep component lists in build files. Repository access runs through SYS-G1. The incoming inspection procedure for boards from the contract manufacturer has no firmware integrity check

title: Transformer Manufacturing: PSIRT procedure and utility addenda register
source_system: PSIRT case system; contracts register
what_it_shows: Public vulnerability intake page; PSIRT coordination procedure with utility security contacts and the contract manufacturer. The addenda register lists 140 utilities that operate medium or high impact BES Cyber Systems, with contacts and terms: 95 require incident notice within 48 hours and 45 within 24 hours; all require notice within 1 business day when a company representative's access should end, vulnerability disclosure within 30 days, hashes or signatures for firmware and patches, and utility-controlled, MFA-protected, per-session remote access. The incident notice step is in the PSIRT procedure and not in the group IR plan, and no exercise of it is recorded

title: Transformer Manufacturing: field service departure checklist and procedures
source_system: Group HR system; field service procedures
what_it_shows: The HR departure checklist was revised in 2026-04 with a step to notify addendum utilities when field staff leave. Field technicians connect only through each utility's remote access system. About 900 field laptops, each with EDR and full-disk encryption

title: Transformer Manufacturing: FMS architecture, release and operations records
source_system: FMS console and deployment pipeline (SYS-M6, provider B)
what_it_shows: About 70 utility subscribers and 18,000 monitored transformers. Utilities push TMU data one way over mutually authenticated TLS; the FMS has no inbound path to utility networks or TMUs. Component inventory and data flow diagram on file. Multi-tenant database with application-level tenant isolation; isolation tests are run by hand and recorded in release test records. Application changes are gated in the deployment pipeline; AI-003 model and configuration changes are released outside the gate. Capacity monitoring and autoscaling; audit configuration on; backups to the vault and a warm standby region that has not been failed over in a test. Subscription agreements state no security, availability or notice commitments; there is no system description and no deletion procedure for departing subscribers. Subscribers asked for a SOC 2 Type 2 report in 2026

title: Transformer Manufacturing: federal contract files, covered system list and SAM.gov reviews
source_system: Federal contracts office records
what_it_shows: 14 civilian federal contracts (no DoD), about $210 million of backlog, all with FAR 52.204-21, 52.204-23 and 52.204-25; the 9 awarded since 2024 also include 52.204-30. Covered contractor information systems scoped 2025-11: GEPS, PLM, TDMS, SYS-G1, SYS-G6 and the project sites for the 14 contracts; P8 performs no federal work. FCI labels on 9 of 14 contract folders, with restricted project sites for those 9. Engineering and installation subcontracts carry the 52.204-21(c) flow-down. SAM.gov reviews in 2026-01 and 2026-04 found no applicable orders

title: Transformer Manufacturing: physical security and facility records
source_system: Badge and CCTV systems; facility management records
what_it_shows: Badge access, visitor sign-in and escort, badge logs and CCTV at the 8 plants, offices and the 3 spare transformer yards; the yards are fenced and patrolled, with intrusion detection at 2 of 3. Generators and hurricane hardening at the plants and the group data center (P1, P2 and the data center are in Florida). Media sanitization certificates for retired drives and wiped laptops. Public website content is approved by communications under the web publishing procedure

title: Transformer Manufacturing: export classification, product line and bid gate records
source_system: Trade compliance records; bid review gate log
what_it_shows: Products and technology classified EAR99 in the 2025 review by the Director of trade compliance. The product lines contain no vehicles or vehicle connectivity systems. The bid review gate, in place since 2025, stops any bid that would flow down DFARS 252.204-7012 or a CMMC level until the group executive risk committee approves a compliance plan; 1 bid was declined in 2026-04

title: Transformer Manufacturing: demand planning and storm allocation records
source_system: GEPS APS and demand planning records; AI-001 model registry
owner: VP supply chain and demand planning
what_it_shows: AI-001 forecasts set the number of storm-reserve production slots and spare units held from June to November, including slots for the affiliated Electric Utility. A storm allocation committee (VP supply chain, VP manufacturing operations, counsel) approves allocations; no written allocation rule and no documented affiliate share were provided. AI-001 retraining is not recorded as a change. Planners review the forecast monthly. Large power transformer backlog about 30 months; distribution backlog about 24 weeks. Each plant MES holds about 48 hours of released work orders

title: Transformer Manufacturing: TDMS and PLM records
source_system: TDMS and PLM administration consoles (SYS-M3, SYS-M4)
what_it_shows: TDMS runs in provider A with backups in the vault; test stations keep local results for 30 days; TDMS integrity checks are limited to database backups; every certified test report carries quality review and signatures. PLM access is broad within engineering, bulk exports raise no alert, and customer NDA drawings are not tagged in PLM

title: Transformer Manufacturing: supplier master change procedure
source_system: Accounts payable procedures (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: Supplier bank detail changes are approved by email, with call-back verification for changes over $250,000

title: Electric Utility: CIP-002-5.1a categorization records
source_system: NERC compliance records
what_it_shows: Registered as DP, TO and TOP in the SERC region. Categorization record approved 2025-11-18: medium impact BES Cyber Systems at the TCC and backup TCC (criterion 2.12); low impact at the 58 transmission substations (criterion 3.2); no high impact BES Cyber Systems; no asset meets a Section 1 criterion. New substations are added from the energization checklist. No transmission station meets CIP-014-3 Applicability 4.1.1. The DCCs, distribution SCADA and outage management, AMI, the CIS and the 310 distribution substations are outside CIP scope

title: Electric Utility: CIP-003-9 policies, CIP Senior Manager record and Transient Cyber Asset plan
source_system: NERC compliance records
what_it_shows: CIP Senior Manager: the senior vice president of transmission and distribution operations; change log current. The medium impact policy covers the nine Part 1.1 topics and was approved by the CIP Senior Manager in 2026-02; the low impact policy covers the Part 1.2 topics, including 1.2.6 vendor electronic remote access. The Transient Cyber Asset plan accepts devices managed by Grid Engineering and 3 relay vendors on the basis of their own procedures, with no documented review

title: Electric Utility: low impact substation vendor access records
source_system: Utility remote access system; sensor deployment list
what_it_shows: Vendor sessions to the 58 transmission substations run only through the utility remote access system with MFA, which records who connected and when. Detection sensors on the vendor remote access path are deployed at 22 of the 58 substations; the other 36 have session recording only

title: Electric Utility: TCC CIP-005-7 to CIP-007-6 records
source_system: Electronic Access Point and Intermediate System configurations; physical security plan; patch, antimalware and logging records
what_it_shows: ESP diagrams and EAP firewall exports: all External Routable Connectivity to the TCC passes through identified EAPs with deny-by-default rules; the corporate network can reach the EAP, where rules block it; Interactive Remote Access through the Intermediate System with MFA, with encryption ending there; group SOC sensors at the EAPs. Physical security plan for the TCC and backup TCC with badge control, monitoring and alarm tests. Patch evaluations every 35 days since the 2025 mitigation; antimalware on applicable Cyber Assets with signatures updated through the Intermediate System; security event logging with alerts, 1 year kept. The DCC has no OT network sensors

title: Electric Utility: TCC CIP-009-6 to CIP-011-3 records
source_system: NERC compliance records; change records
what_it_shows: Recovery plans for the TCC and backup TCC with backup and verification processes, tested 2025-10 with a representative backup sample. Baselines, change authorization and updates within 30 days since the 2025 mitigation; software source and integrity verified before changes when the vendor provides a method. The information protection program defines the BCSI identification method, keeps BCSI in the utility repository and excludes BCSI from the GEPS and the EAM

title: Electric Utility: CIP-004-7 program records
